story.conflict: The neighbor insists they were both assigned the same parking space, reports the narrator for harassment, and uses an edited lease screenshot to make management treat the dispute as a clerical error.
story.hook: My neighbor reported me to management for threatening to tow her car out of the parking space I pay for.
story.premise: A resident keeps finding a neighbor's SUV in her paid apartment parking space, only to discover the neighbor rented out her own assigned spot for cash and falsified a lease screenshot so she could take someone else's space for free.
story.punchline: You sold your own space and tried to take mine.
story.script:
I had just moved into my apartment, and my lease clearly listed parking space 47 as mine. For the first week, everything was fine. Then I came home after work and found a white SUV sitting in it.

I left a polite note and parked in visitor parking. The next night, the SUV was back. This time the owner was standing beside it. She lived two doors down and told me I needed to stop leaving ‘aggressive notes’ because space 47 was hers too.

I thought she had the wrong number, until she pulled out her phone and showed me a screenshot of her lease. Right there, under parking, it said 47.

Management told us there might have been a clerical error during a recent system migration. Until they sorted it out, they asked us to ‘work it out between ourselves.’ Somehow, that meant I kept using visitor parking while she kept using my reserved space.

Then she reported me for harassment after I said I would call the building’s approved tow service the next time her car was there. She even posted in the residents’ group chat that I was trying to steal a parking space from a single woman living alone.

That was when I stopped arguing and started documenting everything.

I photographed my lease, the garage map, every visitor-parking receipt, and every night her SUV was in 47. While checking the garage map, I noticed something strange: her actual unit was assigned space 52.

But space 52 was never empty. The same blue hatchback was there every weekday.

A few evenings later, I saw her meeting a man beside 52. She handed him a garage remote, he handed her an envelope, and they walked away in opposite directions.

I sent management one email with the dates and asked them to check the original lease records instead of screenshots.

The next morning, they called me downstairs.

Her signed lease had always said 52. The screenshot showing 47 had been edited. Security footage also showed the blue hatchback owner using her garage remote for weeks. She had quietly rented out her real space for cash, then claimed mine so she could still park for free.

Management revoked the extra remote, ordered her SUV out of 47, and reimbursed every visitor-parking charge I had paid.

She tried to tell me it was all a misunderstanding.

I just looked at her and said, ‘You sold your own space and tried to take mine.’

She never posted about me in the group chat again.
story.twist: The neighbor's real assigned space was being secretly rented to another driver for cash, and the screenshot claiming the narrator's space had been digitally altered.

youtube.title: She Kept Taking My Parking Spot—Then I Found Out Why
